label: John 4:1
text: Therefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John

label: John 4:2
text: (although Jesus himself didn’t baptize, but his disciples),

label: John 4:3
text: he left Judea, and departed into Galilee.

label: John 4:4
text: He needed to pass through Samaria.

label: John 4:5
text: So he came to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son, Joseph.

label: John 4:6
text: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

label: John 4:7
text:
A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her,
“Give me a drink.”

label: John 4:8
text: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

label: John 4:9
text: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

variants.reading: the clause 'for Jews have no dealings with Samaritans' omitted
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:9): ου γαρ συγχρωνται Ιουδαιοι Σαμαριταις ('for Jews have no association with Samaritans') omitted by א* D it a,b,d,e,j cop fay; the original hand of Sinaiticus omits it. Codex Bezae (D) has no node in the graph.

label: John 4:10
text:
Jesus answered her,
“If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

label: John 4:11
text: The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water?

label: John 4:12
text: Are you greater than our father, Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank of it himself, as did his children, and his livestock?”

label: John 4:13
text:
Jesus answered her,
“Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,

label: John 4:14
text: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

label: John 4:15
text: The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”

label: John 4:16
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Go, call your husband, and come here.”

label: John 4:17
text:
The woman answered, “I have no husband.”
Jesus said to her,
“You said well, ‘I have no husband,’

label: John 4:18
text: for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”

label: John 4:19
text: The woman said to him, “Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.

label: John 4:20
text: Our fathers worshiped in this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship.”

label: John 4:21
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, will you worship the Father.

label: John 4:22
text: You worship that which you don’t know. We worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.

label: John 4:23
text: But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshipers.

label: John 4:24
text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

label: John 4:25
text: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah comes, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”

label: John 4:26
text:
Jesus said to her,
“I am he, the one who speaks to you.”

label: John 4:27
text: At this, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”

label: John 4:28
text: So the woman left her water pot, and went away into the city, and said to the people,

label: John 4:29
text: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I did. Can this be the Christ?”

label: John 4:30
text: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

label: John 4:31
text: In the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”

label: John 4:32
text:
But he said to them,
“I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”

label: John 4:33
text: The disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?”

label: John 4:34
text:
Jesus said to them,
“My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.

label: John 4:35
text: Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest?’ Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes, and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.

label: John 4:36
text: He who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit to eternal life; that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.

label: John 4:37
text: For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:37): 'Verse omitted in P75'. The WEB prints the verse, so no preserves edge runs from artifact:papyrus-75 to this passage.

label: John 4:38
text: I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”

label: John 4:39
text: From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I did.”

label: John 4:40
text: So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.

label: John 4:41
text: Many more believed because of his word.

label: John 4:42
text: They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:42): 'the Christ' omitted in P66 P75 א B C* W supp 083 vid, present in the Byzantine text the WEB follows ('indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world').

label: John 4:43
text: After the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee.

label: John 4:44
text: For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.

label: John 4:45
text: So when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.

label: John 4:46
text: Jesus came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:46): 'Jesus' present in A Θ Ψ f1,13 Byz, omitted in P66 P75 א B C* W supp 086 33 1241; a minor variation, recorded for completeness.

label: John 4:47
text: When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him, and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.

label: John 4:48
text:
Jesus therefore said to him,
“Unless you see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.”

label: John 4:49
text: The nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”

label: John 4:50
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.

label: John 4:51
text: As he was now going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!”

label: John 4:52
text: So he inquired of them the hour when he began to get better. They said therefore to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him.”

label: John 4:53
text:
So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him,
“Your son lives.” He believed, as did his whole house.

variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of John (John 4:53): 'Jesus' omitted in the original hand of א* and N*, present in the remaining witnesses; N (Codex Purpureus) has no node in the graph.

label: John 4:54
text: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee.

label: Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
statement: The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John, although Jesus himself did not baptize but his disciples did.

label: Jesus left Judea for Galilee and had to pass through Samaria
statement: Jesus left Judea and departed into Galilee, and he needed to pass through Samaria.

label: Jesus came to a city of Samaria called Sychar
statement: Jesus came to a city of Samaria called Sychar. Sychar is otherwise unknown; it is debated whether it is Shechem or a nearby village.
note: Identification disputed: Shechem (Tell Balata) or a village near Mount Ebal (often connected with Askar); see docs/seed-leads-john.md and the attests edges.

label: Sychar was near the parcel of ground Jacob gave to his son Joseph
statement: Sychar lay near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph, the ground biblical scholars identify with the plot Jacob bought 'within sight' of Shechem (Genesis 33).

label: Jacob's well was there, and Jesus sat down by it about the sixth hour
statement: Jacob's well was there; Jesus, tired from the journey, sat down by the well about the sixth hour (noon).

label: Jews have no dealings with Samaritans
statement: 'For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans' - the narrator's explanation of the woman's surprise that a Jew would ask a Samaritan for a drink; mutual avoidance between Jews and Samaritans.
note: The clause is itself a variant omission in א* D; see the passage node. The claim is the stated custom, not the conversation.

label: Our fathers worshiped in this mountain; you Jews say Jerusalem is the place to worship
statement: The Samaritan woman says the fathers worshiped 'in this mountain' (Mount Gerizim) while the Jews hold that Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship - ancestral Samaritan worship centered on the Gerizim temple against the Jerusalem temple.

label: The Samaritan woman expects the Messiah ('I know that Messiah comes')
statement: The woman says 'I know that Messiah comes (he who is called Christ). When he has come, he will declare to us all things' - Messianic expectation among Samaritans.

label: 'There are yet four months until the harvest'
statement: Jesus quotes a farm saying, 'Don't you say, there are yet four months until the harvest?' - roughly the interval between sowing and harvest in the grain agriculture of the region.

label: Many Samaritans of the city believed and Jesus stayed two days
statement: Many Samaritans of that city believed because of the woman's testimony; after he stayed two days many more believed, and they said 'this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world'.

label: The Galileans received him, having seen what he did at the feast, for they also went to the feast
statement: Galileans had gone up to the feast in Jerusalem and received Jesus in Galilee because they had seen what he did there - Galilean pilgrimage to the Jerusalem festivals.

label: Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water wine
statement: Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, the village where (John 2:1-11) he had made the water into wine. Cana appears in John only (2:1, 11; 4:46; 21:2); its site is debated (Khirbet Qana vs Kafr Kanna).
note: The brief said to reuse Cana from John 2, but data/john/02 is not yet built, so this chapter creates place:cana; the John 2 runner should copy it byte-for-byte. The site debate (Khirbet Qana vs Kafr Kanna) is John 2's assignment.

label: A royal official (basilikos) whose son was sick at Capernaum begged Jesus to heal him
statement: A certain royal official (basilikos), whose son lay sick at Capernaum at the point of death, heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee and begged him to come down and heal his son. The word basilikos suggests an officer of a royal court - plausibly the tetrarch Antipas's, though the emperor's service is also argued.

label: The son was healed at the seventh hour, the very hour Jesus spoke
statement: Jesus said 'Go, your son lives'; the man believed and went, his servants met him reporting the son lived, and the fever had left him yesterday at the seventh hour - the very hour Jesus spoke. The father and his whole house believed.

label: Sychar
modern_name: possibly Shechem (Tell Balata) or a village under Mount Ebal, e.g. Askar

label: Jacob's Well (Bir Ya'qub) at Balata, Nablus
periods: ancient rock-cut well; Byzantine church by 384 CE; Crusader church 1175; present Greek Orthodox St. Photini church

label: Josephus on Hyrcanus taking Shechem and Gerizim and the temple deserted
author: Josephus

label: Wikipedia: Jacob's Well (location at Bir Ya'qub)
title: Wikipedia: Jacob's Well
excerpt: Jacob's Well is located 76 meters (249 ft) from Tell Balata in the eastern part of the city of Nablus within the grounds of the Bir Ya'qub monastery.

label: Wikipedia: Jacob's Well (identification by the 330s CE)
title: Wikipedia: Jacob's Well
excerpt: By the 330s AD, the site had been identified as the place where Jesus held his conversation with the Samaritan woman, and was probably being used for Christian baptisms.

label: Wikipedia: Shechem (the Sychar identification debate)
title: Wikipedia: Shechem
excerpt: It is not known whether the Samaritan city of Sychar ( Ancient Greek : Συχάρ , romanized : Sykhár ) in the Gospel of John ( John 4:5 ) refers to Shechem or to another nearby village:

label: Wikipedia: Shechem (identified with Tell Balata)
title: Wikipedia: Shechem
excerpt: Shechem is now identified with the nearby site of Tell Balata in Balata village in the West Bank, Palestine.

label: Wikipedia: Cana (John 4:46 reference)
title: Wikipedia: Cana
excerpt: The other biblical references to Cana are also in John: John 4 ( John 4:46 ), which mentions that Jesus is visiting Cana when he is asked to heal the son of a royal official at Capernaum

label: Wikipedia: Healing the royal official's son (the basilikos)
title: Wikipedia: Healing the royal official's son
excerpt: The official, based in Capernaum, may have been in service to either the tetrarch Herod Antipas or the emperor. It is not clear whether he is a Jew or Gentile.

label: Wikipedia: Healing the royal official's son (relation to the centurion)
title: Wikipedia: Healing the royal official's son
excerpt: A similar episode appears in Matthew 8:5–13 and Luke 7:1–10, where a Centurion's slave / servant is healed. While Fred Craddock treats these as the same miracle, R.T. France considers them separate events.

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 13 (Hyrcanus takes Shechem and Gerizim)
title: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 13
excerpt: After this he took Samega, and the neighboring places; and besides these, Shechem and Gerizzim, and the nation of the Cutheans, who dwelt at the temple which resembled that temple which was at Jerusalem

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 13 (the Gerizim temple deserted)
title: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 13
excerpt: which temple was now deserted two hundred years after it was built

label: Wikipedia: Joseph's Tomb (the Madaba Map legend 'Joseph's')
title: Wikipedia: Joseph's Tomb
excerpt: The Madaba Mosaic Map (6th century) designates a site somewhat problematically with the legend – "Joseph's" (τὸ τοῦ Ὶωσήφ) – where the usual adjective 'holy' ( hagios ) accompanying mentions of saints and their shrines is lacking.

label: Wikipedia: Samaritans (the Taheb expectation)
title: Wikipedia: Samaritans
excerpt: Many Samaritans believe that at the end of days, the dead will be resurrected by the Taheb, a restorer (possibly a prophet, some say Moses).

label: Wikipedia: Samaritans (Gerizim as the one true sanctuary)
title: Wikipedia: Samaritans
excerpt: Mount Gerizim, not Jerusalem, is the one true sanctuary chosen by Israel's God.
